newsitem.title: UK: Laporte gains after first-half results.
newsitem.headline: Laporte gains after first-half results.

text.p: Shares in Laporte Plc were marked higher in early trading on Monday after the chemical company posted a drop in first-half pre-tax profit but said the results of its restructuring programme were showing through.
The stock was up 11p at 750 by 0709 GMT.
Chief executive Jim Leng said: "The vigorous action plan to rationalise and refocus the group is now well underway with considerable progress being achieved."
Analysts said the results looked towards the top end of analyst expectations but said Leng's comments on the restructuring benefits were offset by continued weak demand in continental Europe.

"The figures look to be at the top of the range but if you look at the statement the company is saying European markets will remain competitive and are not expected to pick up," said one analyst, who asked not to be named.
"We will probably nudge up our 1996 estimates but we will want to see what the company says at the meeting this morning," the analyst said.

"Obviously the new management team has only been in place since July and has not yet had a chance to really get its teeth into things but it will be interesting to see how much scope there is for cost-cutting in the second half."
In his statement, Leng said challenging market conditions continued and activity in Europe was less robust than in the prior six months.
But he said the latest results showed a significant advance on the second half of the previous year and considrable progress was being achieved in the company's restructuring programme.
Laporte posted a 46 percent drop in first-half pre-tax profits to 36.4 million stg after exceptional items from 67.0 million stg a year ago.
